title: MIT Biology Major Foundations: Introductory Biology, Genetics, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, and Molecular Biology

sources.notes: MIT OCW 7.012 course identity for core biochemistry, genetics, molecular biology, cell biology, molecular-level biological function, gene structure/regulation, protein synthesis, cells, multicellular systems, organisms, research in cell biology, immunology, neurobiology, developmental biology, and ecology.

MIT OCW 7.013 course identity for introductory biology core material with genomic approaches to human biology, neuroscience, development, immunology, tissue repair, stem cells, tissue engineering, infectious disease, inherited disease, cancer, recitations, problem sets, solutions, and exams.

MIT OCW 7.016 course identity for fundamental principles of biochemistry, molecular biology, and genetics, living-system function, chemical biology, twenty-first-century molecular genetics, human health, therapeutic intervention, recitations, problem sets, solutions, and exams.

MIT OCW 7.03 Genetics course identity for molecules, cells, multicellular organisms, humans, genes, chromosomes, genomes, recombination, mutation, selection, population genetics, genetic analysis of protein function, gene regulation, inherited disease, readings, problem sets, and exams.

MIT OCW 7.03 syllabus identity for genetics meeting pattern, recommended textbook, NCBI/PubMed and online textbook boundaries, graded problem sets, collaboration policy, exams, and solution boundaries.

MIT OCW 7.05 General Biochemistry course identity for cell/tissue/organism structure and function, nucleic acids, proteins, carbohydrates, enzymology, biochemical mechanisms, macromolecular synthesis/degradation, signaling, transport, movement, carbohydrate/fat/nitrogen metabolism, recitations, assignments, exams, and quizzes.

MIT OCW 7.05 syllabus identity for introductory biology prerequisites, OCW Scholar linkage, biochemistry course description, lecture/recitation meetings, assignments, exams, quizzes, textbook/readings, and course-material boundaries.

MIT OCW RES.7-007 / 7.06x Cell Biology course identity for higher-organism cells, membranes, organelles, cell growth, oncogenic transformation, transport, receptors, signaling, cytoskeleton, extracellular matrix, cell movement, cell division/cycle, specialized cell types, molecular knowledge, experimental approaches, videos, problem sets, and solution boundaries.

MIT OCW RES.7-008 / 7.28x Molecular Biology course identity for genome maintenance/expression/evolution, prokaryotic and eukaryotic genomes, gene regulation, DNA replication, genetic recombination, transcription, mRNA translation, experimental design, data analysis, MITx series, lecture, reading, and quiz boundaries.
